title: The bass as foundation; club owners cutting bands
summary: Drum, bass and piano are the foundation; owners cut bands from six to five when union scale rises, dropping bass or trombone.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, what's the foundation of a band? That's what I'm really getting at.
Well, I think the foundation of a band? Drum, bass, and piano. That's your foundation. That's what gives it its depth.

I don't know. I think it was Bill Cray, somebody like that, or Leonard Ferguson, one of the guys, musicians that I've talked to, saying that all nightclub owners want to get rid of bass. They don't understand the importance of it, you know. No, I don't. And he was saying how important the bass is.

I don't agree with that. Not all nightclubers want to. I'll tell you where you might have misunderstood them. It's not the nightclub owners want to get rid of the bass. It's because to a band leader, your drum, bass, and piano are three important instruments. You're a foundation. We're supplying the bottom, and we're giving it the drive and the depth. And where you may have gotten the wrong opinion, usually when the unions raise the scale on these steady band leaders, and you have a six-piece band, and they're playing six nights a week and one night off, which we have to have because of union rules. And every time the union votes a raise every year, every other year, something like that, and you have a six-piece band in this club, well, I think most of the time out of Spike, the club owners just for Spike will cut the band down to five men. And they usually either cut out the trombone or the bass, but they don't tell the band leader who to cut out. They'll say, we're going to cut you down to five men, just to save those few dollars because of the raise. And then three or four months later, they usually bill it back to six men again. But I sometimes think they do it for Spike, because it's the musicians that's making the money for them. We're bringing in their profits. Oh, yeah. And they seem to realize that months later, they're back to six men again.
Well, some people just don't appreciate what good time is, either.
